text:
Elaine Park: Heads up — SIEM spiking on the "API Key Creation (prod)" rule since 05:00 UTC. ~430 alerts in 3 hours, ~95% look like our CI service accounts. Noticed a repeat source IP range and identical user_agent strings.
sec-bot: [alert] Rule="API Key Creation (prod)" count=432 window=3h severity=medium
Raj Patel: thanks for flagging. do we have a sample of the events? can you paste a sanitized example (cloudtrail/okta/etc)?
Elaine Park: here's a sanitized CloudTrail JSON snippet we pulled from one alert: ```{ "eventName": "CreateApiKey", "userIdentity": { "type": "AssumedRole", "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ci-deploy/gha" }, "sourceIPAddress": "54.12.34.56", "userAgent": "github-actions/2.284.0" }``` most hits match this pattern.
Omar Diaz: looks like the rule is too generic — it fires on any CreateApiKey event in prod. our CI automation legitimately creates ephemeral keys during deploys. we should match on userIdentity or userAgent to reduce noise.
Raj Patel: Agreed. Proposal: update SIEM detection to exclude `AssumedRole` with role name pattern `ci-*` and userAgent containing `github-actions`. Also add an allowlist for known IP ranges used by CI.
Maria Chen: I can update the dashboard and tag alerts as "known-ci" once rule changes land. Can we also add a visualization showing top 10 userAgents for this rule? will help verify tuning.
Elaine Park: +1. quick patch plan: 1) suppress existing alerts matching CI pattern for 7 days, 2) change rule to exclude CI patterns and add a threshold (>=3 unique principals in 5m) before paging, 3) add dashboard split, 4) add note to playbook. Who owns 1-3?
Raj Patel: I'll push the rule change. Suggested KQL for the exclusion (SIEM syntactic example): ```eventName == "CreateApiKey" and not (userIdentity.type == "AssumedRole" and userIdentity.arn contains "assumed-role/ci-") and not userAgent contains "github-actions"``` then wrap with a cardinality check: `| summarize principals = dcount(userIdentity.arn) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m) | where principals >= 3`
Omar Diaz: I'll coordinate with infra to confirm the CI IP ranges and add them to the allowlist. infra will provide CIDR list by EOD.
Elaine Park: Raj — do you have permissions to edit the rule and create a temporary suppression? If not, we can open a rule-change PR.
Raj Patel: I have edit perms for detections. I'll create a rule version `v2-ci-exclusions` and enable in dry-run for 1h, then flip to active after sanity checks. will post the diff in the thread.
sec-bot: [action] rule_update_requested id=det-7783 requester=Raj Patel
Maria Chen: After Raj flips it, I'll run a 2-hour check and update the dashboard tiles. Also creating an annotation on the incident timeline: "False positives traced to CI automation — rule adjusted".
Elaine Park: can we add a short playbook entry so on future spikes folks triage CI-patterns quickly? minimal: check userAgent, assumed-role naming, and cross-ref CI deploy times.
Omar Diaz: I'll draft the playbook snippet and drop in the runbook at <https://confluence.redwood.com/runbooks/siem-keys|Runbook - Key Alerts>. tagging @infra for the CIDR list.
infra-bot: ping infra-team: please provide CI egress CIDRs for allowlist. (automated)
Jacob (infra-team): noted — we have a CSR in progress, pushing CIDRs to #eng-infra within 2 hours.
Raj Patel: Rule diff (dry-run): ```- condition: eventName == "CreateApiKey" + condition: eventName == "CreateApiKey" and not (userIdentity.type == "AssumedRole" and userIdentity.arn matches "assumed-role/ci-*") and not userAgent contains "github-actions"``` enabling cardinality filter as second stage. will enable dry-run at 17:40 UTC.
Elaine Park: sounds good. Action items: Raj (rule change + dry-run), Omar (CI IPs + playbook draft), Maria (dashboard + annotation), Raj/Elaine (post-mortem note). Let's reconvene in 3 hours or earlier if noise persists. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: noted. I'll update the incident entry and tag for follow-up in the weekly SIEM tuning review.
Raj Patel: dry-run enabled. monitoring noise now — will report counts in 30m.
sec-bot: [alert] Rule="API Key Creation (prod)" dry_run_count=12 window=1h
Elaine Park: thanks all. if dry-run holds (low counts), we'll flip and close suppression. if not, escalate to broader detection revamp. closing loop in thread later.
